title: Paid reservations: Even-key census
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: Each reservation is [start,end,reward], with start < end and nonnegative reward, occupying [start,end). Sort by end, then start, then reward. For each nonempty prefix of this sorted list, produce the maximum reward from nonoverlapping reservations in that prefix. Touching endpoints are compatible. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
Reward-bearing reservation cards require a prefix account that weighs payment against compatible earlier work. Alma separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

Each reservation is [start,end,reward], with start < end and nonnegative reward, occupying [start,end). Sort by end, then start, then reward. For each nonempty prefix of this sorted list, produce the maximum reward from nonoverlapping reservations in that prefix. Touching endpoints are compatible.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement paidReservationsEvenKeyCensus(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.

referenceSolutions.python:
def paidReservationsEvenKeyCensus(drawers, k):
    a=drawers
    out=[]
    rows=sorted(a,key=lambda r:(r[1],r[0],r[2]))
    dp=[0]
    for i,(start,end,reward) in enumerate(rows):
        left,right=0,i
        while left<right:
            mid=(left+right)//2
            if rows[mid][1]<=start: left=mid+1
            else: right=mid
        dp.append(max(dp[i],dp[left]+reward))
    out=dp[1:]
    return sum(x%2==0 for x in out)
